quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You see a green traffic light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter until you can drive all the way across.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter until you can drive all the way across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can drive completely through before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and give the right-of-way to others.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Stay parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest edge.

questions.question: Bad suspension in your car can cause:

options.text: Loss of vehicle control.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of vehicle control.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives a smooth ride on different road surfaces. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Drive more slowly.
Look around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss in blind spots or quick glances. Always look for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters while driving.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Wait for the green light.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be alert, and proceed with care. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: Your vehicle starts to skid. What should you do?

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake hard.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to regain control. Steer in the direction of the skid to help straighten out the vehicle.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, you should drive at:

options.text: The same speed as freeway traffic or close to it.
The posted speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as freeway traffic or close to it.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must stop for other traffic.
Traffic is merging in. Leave space so drivers can safely merge into traffic.
Traffic is merging in. Stay in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging in. Leave space so drivers can safely merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead. Check your mirrors and sides, then move to another lane if possible to give merging drivers a clear path.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, and go when safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger car.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than cars, so you need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles have only one tail light, making them hard to see at night.

questions.question: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day because:

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery.
Your reaction time is slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: Low light and headlight glare reduce how far you can see at night compared to daytime. Always use headlights and be careful when driving in the dark.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lane markings mean:

options.text: No one can pass.
Both lanes can pass.
The right lane can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate traffic going in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Allow a larger following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a three- to four-second distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop very quickly. If the motorcyclist falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting them. Falls are most common on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. A person may open a door or step out without looking. A parked car may start moving without seeing you.

questions.question: A sign with this shape means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn permitted on red.
Yield right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks the start of a no passing zone.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, remove your foot from the gas pedal. Let the vehicle slow down gradually. Use the brakes lightly only after the vehicle has slowed a lot.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line marking:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: You want to park downhill on a two-way road and there is no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill or uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels toward the center so the car will roll into the curb.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a collision scene.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a collision scene.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at accidents causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: You can help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away from your vehicle by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Maintaining a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintaining a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Help drivers behind you stay a safe distance away by driving at a steady speed. Also, signal turns, lane changes, and when you are slowing down.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. Dry, solid surfaces are safest for driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching you.
Come to a full stop then proceed when it is safe to do so.
Proceed carefully through the intersection, not always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop then proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Stop at the marked stop line and go only when it is safe. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop at a point where you can see all traffic.
